sentences.en: To subvert the tyranny of our execrable government, to break the connection with England, the never-failing source of all our political evils,
sentences.zh: 为了颠覆我们那可恶政府的暴政，为了切断与英国——我们所有政治弊端的万恶之源——的联系，

sentences.en: and to assert the independence of my country, these were my objects.
sentences.zh: 并主张我祖国的独立，这些就是我的目标。

sentences.en: To unite the whole people of Ireland, to abolish the memory of all past dissensions, and to substitute the common name of Irishman in place of the denominations of Protestant,
sentences.zh: 为了团结全体爱尔兰人民，为了抹去过去所有纷争的记忆，并用“爱尔兰人”这一共同称呼，来取代新教徒、

sentences.en: Catholic, and dissenter.
sentences.zh: 天主教徒和异见者这些教派名称。

sentences.en: These were my means.
sentences.zh: 这些就是我的手段。

sentences.en: So those, Tom Holland, are the words of Wolfe Tone, and last time on The Rest is History, when we were doing our epic sweep through the interwoven histories of Ireland, England,
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰，以上就是沃尔夫·托恩的话。上次在《历史的余韵》节目中，当我们对爱尔兰、英格兰

sentences.en: and Britain, we were joined by Paul Rouse from University College Dublin, and it's delightful for us, isn't it, that Paul is back, and we're still in the GPO.
sentences.zh: 和英国之间交织的历史进行宏大回顾时，都柏林大学学院的保罗·劳斯加入了我们。保罗能回来真是太好了，对吧？而且我们现在还在邮政总局（GPO）。

sentences.en: We're still in the GPO, yes.
sentences.zh: 我们确实还在邮政总局。

sentences.en: In the centrepiece of the Easter Rising, so Paul, welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 在复活节起义的核心地带。所以，保罗，欢迎回到《历史的余韵》。

sentences.en: Thanks a million, Donald.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，唐纳德。

sentences.en: I mean, for everybody else, you've been gone for three days.
sentences.zh: 我是说，对其他人来说，你已经离开三天了。

sentences.en: For us, you, I mean, it's actually three minutes this week, the last episode.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说，也就是这周的三分钟，上一集刚结束。

sentences.en: But we ended last time with the 1798 Rebellion, Wolfe Tone, the interplay of republicanism, romanticism, revolution and religion in Irish society, and the Act of Union.
sentences.zh: 但上次我们结束时谈到了1798年叛乱、沃尔夫·托恩、爱尔兰社会中共和主义、浪漫主义、革命与宗教的相互作用，以及《联合法案》。

sentences.en: So Ireland is now part of, as a reaction to that failed uprising, Ireland is now part of a united kingdom of Britain and Ireland.
sentences.zh: 所以，作为对那次失败起义的反应，爱尔兰现在成了大不列颠及爱尔兰联合王国的一部分。

sentences.en: And, well, why doesn't it work?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么它行不通呢？

sentences.en: Or does it work, actually, in a way that we perhaps don't appreciate today?
sentences.zh: 或者说，它其实在某种程度上行得通，只是我们今天没有意识到？

sentences.en: Well, there were a lot of attempts to make it work.
sentences.zh: 嗯，确实有很多尝试想让它行得通。

sentences.en: And a lot of really interesting and progressive things happened over the sweep of 120 years.
sentences.zh: 在120年的跨度里，发生了很多非常有趣且进步的事情。

sentences.en: But ultimately, there was a complete disconnect right at the heart of the Act of Union, which was this idea of Catholic emancipation.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，在《联合法案》的核心存在着一个彻底的脱节，那就是关于“天主教解放”的构想。

sentences.en: And that idea, from the very beginning, the promise that after the Act of Union, Catholics would be allowed to sit in the parliament in Westminster.
sentences.zh: 而那个构想，从一开始就承诺在《联合法案》之后，天主教徒将被允许进入威斯敏斯特议会。

sentences.en: And, of course, this was rejected.
sentences.zh: 当然，这遭到了拒绝。

sentences.en: And it was essentially rejected, even though William Pitt supported it.
sentences.zh: 尽管威廉·皮特支持它，但它本质上还是被否决了。

sentences.en: It was the king, is it?
sentences.zh: 是国王的原因，对吧？

sentences.en: It was the king.
sentences.zh: 是国王。

sentences.en: It was George III.
sentences.zh: 是乔治三世。

sentences.en: And this goes back to coronations and his coronation oath, at his disastrous coronation, which we talked about, Dominic,
sentences.zh: 这要追溯到加冕礼和他那灾难性的加冕誓词，多米尼克，我们之前谈到过，

sentences.en: where everyone was falling over and having breakfast and all kinds of shenanigans going on.
sentences.zh: 当时每个人都摔倒了，还在吃早餐，发生了各种闹剧。

sentences.en: But actually, it has this very, very serious consequence that he refuses to allow Catholic emancipation to go ahead.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这产生了一个非常、非常严重的后果，那就是他拒绝让天主教解放继续进行。

sentences.en: And he was unmoved on it and could not be moved on it.
sentences.zh: 他在这个问题上毫不动摇，也无法被说服。

sentences.en: And it was only in the 1820s when Daniel O'Connell, one fascinating figure in Irish history, and we're here in the General Post Office, the GPO, the seat of Irish Revolution.
sentences.zh: 直到19世纪20年代，丹尼尔·奥康奈尔——爱尔兰历史上的一位迷人人物——才出现。我们现在就在爱尔兰革命的中心——邮政总局（GPO）。

sentences.en: But the street that's outside it is now called O'Connell Street.
sentences.zh: 但外面的那条街现在叫奥康奈尔街。

sentences.en: So tell us about Daniel O'Connell.
sentences.zh: 那么，给我们讲讲丹尼尔·奥康奈尔吧。

sentences.en: So Daniel O'Connell is the liberator.
sentences.zh: 丹尼尔·奥康奈尔是“解放者”。

sentences.en: He began, born in Kerry, right down in Carseveen, the furthest part away from here you could possibly be and not be wet.
sentences.zh: 他出生在凯里郡，就在卡尔西文，那是离这里最远、还没被水淹没的地方。

sentences.en: And he came to be a really brilliant barrister, one of the leading barristers of his day.
sentences.zh: 他后来成为了一名非常出色的律师，是他那个时代顶尖的律师之一。

sentences.en: But he also was a politician who wished to stand in parliament.
sentences.zh: 但他也是一位希望进入议会的政治家。

sentences.en: He wished for Catholic emancipation.
sentences.zh: 他渴望实现天主教解放。

sentences.en: And he founded in 1823 a Catholic association based on the counties of Ireland where they collected things and organised those counties which had been shired by the English and which are now such an important part of Irish administrative life still.
sentences.zh: 1823年，他创立了天主教协会，以爱尔兰各郡为基础，在那里收集物资并组织这些曾被英国人划分郡县的地区，这些郡县至今仍是爱尔兰行政生活中极其重要的一部分。

sentences.en: And a huge part of people's identity in Ireland is a county identity.
sentences.zh: 郡县认同感是爱尔兰人身份认同的巨大组成部分。

sentences.en: I am from Galway.
sentences.zh: 我来自戈尔韦。

sentences.en: Far more than in England.
sentences.zh: 比在英国要强烈得多。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not vaguely comparable.
sentences.zh: 我是说，两者根本没有可比性。

sentences.en: It really matters in Ireland, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 在爱尔兰，这真的很重要，不是吗？

sentences.en: It really matters.
sentences.zh: 真的很重要。

sentences.en: It really matters.
sentences.zh: 真的很重要。

sentences.en: And it matters because of sporting allegiance in the Gallic Athletic Association.
sentences.zh: 而且因为盖尔运动协会的体育忠诚度，它变得更加重要。

sentences.en: But it matters as a basic thing of constituencies for which people are elected to parliament.
sentences.zh: 但它作为人们选举进入议会的选区基础，同样重要。

sentences.en: It matters for local government all across the place.
sentences.zh: 它对各地的地方政府也很重要。

sentences.en: It is fundamental to identity for very many people in Ireland.
sentences.zh: 对于爱尔兰的许多人来说，它是身份认同的根本。

sentences.en: And so it was organised in that and there were showdowns through the 1820s.
sentences.zh: 所以它就是这样组织起来的，在19世纪20年代期间发生过多次对决。

sentences.en: But it ended ultimately when O'Connell, standing for a seat in County Clare and being elected as the MP for County Clare, but of course, then it was up to the government.
sentences.zh: 但最终，当奥康奈尔在克莱尔郡竞选席位并当选为克莱尔郡议员时，事情到了终点，但当然，接下来就看政府的了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He can't take a seat.
sentences.zh: 他无法就职。

sentences.en: He can't take a seat, but he can't.
sentences.zh: 他无法就职，但他确实不能。

sentences.en: So eventually he sawed him down.
sentences.zh: 所以最终他还是被压下去了。

sentences.en: And in 1829, a Catholic emancipation bill was passed through the House of Commons.
sentences.zh: 1829年，天主教解放法案在下议院获得通过。

sentences.en: And that is passed by the Duke of Wellington, who is Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 这是由时任首相威灵顿公爵通过的。

sentences.en: And the Duke of Wellington is also, in a sense, I mean, he is Irish.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，威灵顿公爵本人也是爱尔兰人。

sentences.en: I mean, he notoriously said that just because he, you know, being born in a stable doesn't make you a horse.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他曾有一句名言：出生在马厩里并不代表你就是一匹马。

sentences.en: Which is not the...
sentences.zh: 那不是……

sentences.en: Apparently he didn't say that, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，显然他没说过那句话。

sentences.en: Did he not say that?
sentences.zh: 他没说过吗？

sentences.en: Apparently this is apocryphal.
sentences.zh: 显然这是伪托的。

sentences.en: Is that right, Paul?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗，保罗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's apocryphal.
sentences.zh: 是的，是伪托的。

sentences.en: Oh, it is apocryphal.
sentences.zh: 哦，是伪托的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So much about the Duke of Wellington.
sentences.zh: 关于威灵顿公爵就说这么多。

sentences.en: But, so the Duke of Wellington is a fascinating example of an Irishman who becomes synonymous with Britain, with British victory, Britain's greatest general.
sentences.zh: 但是，威灵顿公爵是一个迷人的例子，他是一个与英国、与英国的胜利、与英国最伟大的将军同义的爱尔兰人。

sentences.en: Oh, and more than that, Tom, he...
sentences.zh: 哦，不仅如此，汤姆，他……

sentences.en: And we'll go there later.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后再谈这个。

sentences.en: I will show you the pitch, one of the oldest cricket pitches in the world,
sentences.zh: 我会带你看那个球场，世界上最古老的板球场之一，

sentences.en: where the first ever organised cricket match in Ireland was played between the gentlemen of Ireland and the military and the Duke of Wellington was playing in that game.
sentences.zh: 在那里举行了爱尔兰有史以来第一场有组织的板球比赛，由爱尔兰绅士队对阵军队，威灵顿公爵当时就在那场比赛中打球。

sentences.en: And there was a monument...
sentences.zh: 而且还有一个纪念碑……

sentences.en: God, he gets up even higher in my...
sentences.zh: 天哪，他在我心中的地位又高了……

sentences.en: There was a monument at the gates to the Phoenix Park.
sentences.zh: 在凤凰公园的门口有一个纪念碑。

sentences.en: If people have been to Dublin, the Phoenix Park is juSt...
sentences.zh: 如果人们去过都柏林，凤凰公园就在……

sentences.en: It's hugely important public space to the city and has been for centuries and standing tall over its entrance is an obelisk, which is a massive monument to the Duke of Wellington,
sentences.zh: 它是这座城市极其重要的公共空间，几个世纪以来一直如此。矗立在入口处的是一座方尖碑，那是威灵顿公爵的巨大纪念碑，

sentences.en: which was constructed in his honour.
sentences.zh: 是为了纪念他而建造的。

sentences.en: And while we're on the subject of monuments, just outside us here was the most famous monument in the city.
sentences.zh: 既然提到了纪念碑，就在我们外面，曾有这座城市最著名的纪念碑。

sentences.en: I say was, was, because it was Horatio Nelson.
sentences.zh: 我说“曾有”，是因为那是霍雷肖·纳尔逊。

sentences.en: Paul, for us, this is a very tragic story, because Nelson is very much a friend of the rest of his history.
sentences.zh: 保罗，对我们来说，这是一个非常悲惨的故事，因为纳尔逊在很大程度上是《历史的余韵》的朋友。

sentences.en: He's probably one of our favourite, I mean, one of our two or three favourite historical characters.
sentences.zh: 他可能是我们最喜欢的历史人物之一，我是说，是我们最喜欢的三四个历史人物之一。

sentences.en: So Tom, in particular, is pumped about Nelson, and it's a big deal for Tom to come to a city that blew up the statue of Nelson.
sentences.zh: 所以汤姆特别推崇纳尔逊，对汤姆来说，来到一个炸毁了纳尔逊雕像的城市是一件大事。

sentences.en: Let's get back to this O'Connell, the Liberator, the Duke of Wellington, the Iron Duke, the man who defeats Napoleon at Waterloo.
sentences.zh: 让我们回到奥康奈尔——那位“解放者”、威灵顿公爵——那位“铁公爵”、在滑铁卢击败拿破仑的人身上。

sentences.en: Are we seeing two sides there of the Anglo-Irish relationship in the 19th century?
sentences.zh: 我们是在那里看到了19世纪英爱关系的两个侧面吗？

sentences.en: What you see in Ireland across the whole of the 19th century is a country which is slowly, it's changing.
sentences.zh: 你在整个19世纪的爱尔兰看到的是一个正在缓慢变化的国家。

sentences.en: It has people within it who are absolutely loyal to empire, who are extremely happy to be part of the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 它内部有人绝对忠于帝国，非常乐意成为联合王国的一部分。

sentences.en: And Catholics, including?
sentences.zh: 包括天主教徒吗？

sentences.en: Including Catholics.
sentences.zh: 包括天主教徒。

sentences.en: A very certain class of Catholic ordinarily, but the broad suede of the population were rural and extremely poor.
sentences.zh: 通常是特定阶层的天主教徒，但广大人口是农村人口，而且极其贫困。

sentences.en: That will come to be of enormous significance later in the century.
sentences.zh: 这在世纪晚些时候将变得意义重大。

sentences.en: A lot of them joined the British Army.
sentences.zh: 他们中很多人加入了英军。

sentences.en: Yeah, there is huge Irish recruitment to the British Army,
sentences.zh: 是的，爱尔兰人大量加入英军，

sentences.en: and this is sometimes presented as evidence of being comfortable within empire and evidence of identification increasingly with what is the army of the empire.
sentences.zh: 这有时被视为他们在帝国中感到舒适的证据，以及越来越认同帝国军队的证据。

sentences.en: But of course, it's rooted often in poverty.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这通常根植于贫困。

sentences.en: Now, there are people who join the army for adventure and for excitement or to get away from home or for all the many reasons why people do everything.
sentences.zh: 当然，也有人为了冒险、为了刺激、为了逃离家庭，或者为了人们做任何事情的各种原因而参军。

sentences.en: It's very often very difficult to judge that.
sentences.zh: 判断这一点通常非常困难。

sentences.en: But there is epic poverty across rural Ireland and urban Ireland too.
sentences.zh: 但整个爱尔兰农村乃至城市都存在着史诗般的贫困。

sentences.en: And there's a certain...
sentences.zh: 而且有一种……

sentences.en: And Ireland at this point, so the early 19th century, has about half the population of Great Britain.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰在这一点上，也就是19世纪初，人口大约是大不列颠的一半。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the population of Ireland grew from about 3 million in 1750 to, on the eve of the famine in 1845, it had risen to about 8.4 million.
sentences.zh: 所以爱尔兰的人口从1750年的约300万，增长到1845年大饥荒前夕，已经上升到约840万。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the famine, perhaps even more than Cromwell's invasion, is perhaps the kind of the darkest blot on the history of Anglo-Irish relations.
sentences.zh: 而大饥荒，也许比克伦威尔的入侵更甚，可能是英爱关系史上最黑暗的污点。

sentences.en: You cannot talk or understand modern Ireland in any shape or form without understanding the famine.
sentences.zh: 如果不了解大饥荒，你就无法以任何形式谈论或理解现代爱尔兰。

sentences.en: You must understand it from what it did in cultural terms, in economic terms, its political legacy is immense, and how it reshaped the population of the country.
sentences.zh: 你必须从它在文化、经济方面的影响，它巨大的政治遗产，以及它如何重塑了国家人口结构的角度去理解它。

sentences.en: So can you talk, just talk us through why it is so devastating, why it has the impact that it does,
sentences.zh: 那么你能谈谈，给我们讲讲为什么它如此具有破坏性，为什么它会产生那样的影响，

sentences.en: and how culpable the British government is in the devastating effects that it has?
sentences.zh: 以及英国政府在它造成的毁灭性后果中负有多大责任？

sentences.en: Okay, and in talking about culpability,
sentences.zh: 好的，在谈论责任时，

sentences.en: you have to be clear that what we're not trying to do here is project back standards and values from a new millennium onto the actions of a government in the middle of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 你必须清楚，我们在这里并不是要将新千年的标准和价值观投射到19世纪中叶政府的行为上。

sentences.en: We must enter that caveat at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 我们必须在开始时就提出这个警告。

sentences.en: No, we judge them by the standards of the mid-19th century.
sentences.zh: 不，我们是用19世纪中叶的标准来评判他们。

sentences.en: Of the period.
sentences.zh: 那个时代的标准。

sentences.en: So the growth of population in Ireland to 8.4 million in 1845 is a massive explosion,
sentences.zh: 所以爱尔兰人口在1845年增长到840万是一次巨大的爆炸，

sentences.en: and it's an explosion which is driven across the entirety of the west of Ireland and the midlands and in rural areas by the subdivision of land and by the spread and the use of the potato.
sentences.zh: 这是一场由土地细分以及马铃薯的推广和使用所驱动的爆炸，遍及爱尔兰西部、中部和农村地区。

sentences.en: So about one and a quarter million families were living on farms of fewer than five acres inland, which is exceptionally tiny, tiny, tiny, really small farms,
sentences.zh: 大约有125万个家庭住在爱尔兰不到五英亩的农场上，这非常小，非常、非常小的农场，

sentences.en: not to call them farMs.
sentences.zh: 甚至不能称之为农场。

sentences.en: And these were farms, and this really matters.
sentences.zh: 这些是农场，这一点真的很重要。

sentences.en: These were farms which were essentially taken, and they were tenants of landlords, of the 5,000 landlords, more or less, who are Anglo-Irish.
sentences.zh: 这些农场基本上是被租用的，他们是地主的佃户，那些大约5000名地主，大多是英裔爱尔兰人。

sentences.en: Or not always so, because we have to be very careful not to be absolute on that, but largely speaking, there are 5,000 families who own this land.
sentences.zh: 或者也不尽然，因为我们必须非常小心，不要对此下绝对的定论，但总的来说，有5000个家庭拥有这些土地。

sentences.en: So by the 1840s, there are about 3 million people who depend on the potato for more than 90% of their calorific intake in any given year.
sentences.zh: 所以到了19世纪40年代，大约有300万人每年超过90%的热量摄入依赖马铃薯。

sentences.en: By the way, the potato was not brought to Ireland by Sir Walter Raleigh.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，马铃薯并不是沃尔特·雷利爵士带到爱尔兰的。

sentences.en: It's a product of the exchange of commerce and culture from Ireland and Spain and Britain and everything to do with that.
sentences.zh: 它是爱尔兰、西班牙、英国之间商业和文化交流的产物，与此相关的一切都是如此。

sentences.en: Just say that in passing.
sentences.zh: 顺便提一下。

sentences.en: Blight descended on Europe and in Ireland, hit the potato crop of 1845.
sentences.zh: 枯萎病席卷了欧洲，并在1845年袭击了爱尔兰的马铃薯作物。

sentences.en: That crop lost, but half of it was destroyed.
sentences.zh: 那年的收成损失了，有一半被毁了。

sentences.en: And there are these extraordinary, just vivid accounts of the smell of rotting potatoes.
sentences.zh: 有一些关于腐烂马铃薯气味的非凡而生动的描述。

sentences.en: And of the absolute despair of people who put their hand into the soil to pull up a potato plant and to feel that disgusting squelch of rotten potato where it had died in the ground as the withering goes on.
sentences.zh: 还有人们伸手进土里拔出马铃薯植株，感受到那种令人作呕的烂马铃薯泥浆，因为它们在地下枯萎死亡时的那种绝对绝望。

sentences.en: The impact then in 1846 was devastating.
sentences.zh: 1846年的影响是毁灭性的。

sentences.en: The entire crop failed.
sentences.zh: 全部作物绝收。

sentences.en: In 1847, there was some improvement, but there was so much limited seed potato available because of the previous two years that not as much had been sold and more was loSt.
sentences.zh: 1847年情况有所好转，但由于前两年的原因，可用的种子马铃薯非常有限，所以播种的不多，损失也更多。

sentences.en: So there's marginal recovery again in 1848, but it was only in 1849 that a normal crop of potatoes was harvested in Ireland.
sentences.zh: 所以1848年又有了微小的恢复，但直到1849年，爱尔兰才收获了正常的马铃薯作物。

sentences.en: In the course of these four years, and we'll take a few months either side of it and years either side of it, about 1 million people died.
sentences.zh: 在这四年期间，我们算上前后几个月和几年，大约有100万人死亡。

sentences.en: Of starvation, of illness.
sentences.zh: 死于饥饿，死于疾病。

sentences.en: In a country that is the richest in the world.
sentences.zh: 在一个世界上最富有的国家里。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And about over a million people emigrated.
sentences.zh: 而且有超过100万人移民。

sentences.en: Some emigrated to Liverpool, to that already developing Irish community in Liverpool, or that Irish community along Tottenham Court Road in London.
sentences.zh: 有些人移民到利物浦，去了利物浦那个已经形成的爱尔兰社区，或者伦敦托特纳姆法院路沿线的那个爱尔兰社区。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Or some went on ships, later renamed Coffin Ships.
sentences.zh: 或者有些人登上了后来被称为“棺材船”的船只。

sentences.en: To America.
sentences.zh: 前往美国。

sentences.en: To America and to Canada.
sentences.zh: 前往美国和加拿大。

sentences.en: They stopped at Gross Eel or in Ellis Island, and these become extremely important places in Irish history.
sentences.zh: 他们在格罗斯岛或埃利斯岛停留，这些地方成为了爱尔兰历史上极其重要的地方。

sentences.en: The Irish emigrants who go to America take with them the absolute conviction that the British are responsible for this.
sentences.zh: 前往美国的爱尔兰移民带着一种绝对的信念，那就是英国人对此负有责任。

sentences.en: Oh yeah, this really matters.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，这真的很重要。

sentences.en: See it as a deliberate act of genocide.
sentences.zh: 将其视为一场蓄意的种族灭绝行为。

sentences.en: This really matters.
sentences.zh: 这真的很重要。

sentences.en: So is that true?
sentences.zh: 那么这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Well, you have to see what happened during the famine.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你得看看大饥荒期间发生了什么。

sentences.en: So the prime ministers who held office during the famine were Sir Robert Peel and Lord John Russell.
sentences.zh: 当时在大饥荒期间担任首相的是罗伯特·皮尔爵士和约翰·罗素勋爵。

sentences.en: So in the beginning, the government offered for reliance on the provision of employment through public work schemes in Ireland, the building roads, etc.
sentences.zh: 起初，政府提议通过爱尔兰的公共工程计划来提供就业，比如修路等等，以此作为救济手段。

sentences.en: The cost of which was to be split between local taxpayers and the central government.
sentences.zh: 这些工程的费用由当地纳税人和中央政府分摊。

sentences.en: And at their height in the spring of 1847, there were about 700,000 people, or one in 12 of the population were employed in these schemes.
sentences.zh: 在1847年春季的高峰期，大约有70万人，也就是十二分之一的爱尔兰人口参与了这些计划。

sentences.en: So there's no denying that that was...
sentences.zh: 所以不可否认的是……

sentences.en: So it's kind of like workhouses are operating in England.
sentences.zh: 这有点像英国当时实行的济贫院制度。

sentences.en: And the workhouses come into this story in a minute.
sentences.zh: 稍后我们就会谈到济贫院。

sentences.en: Then the public work schemes were displaced in 1847 by publicly financed soup kitchens.
sentences.zh: 随后，公共工程计划在1847年被政府资助的施粥处所取代。

sentences.en: And these soup kitchens during 1847 were feeding three million daily, which is an enormous undertaking.
sentences.zh: 1847年期间，这些施粥处每天要喂饱三百万人，这是一项巨大的工程。

sentences.en: But the government retreated from the provision of those by the October 1847.
sentences.zh: 但政府在1847年10月就停止了这项供应。

sentences.en: Every soup kitchen was gone and it was left to the workhouses.
sentences.zh: 所有的施粥处都被撤销了，重担又落回了济贫院身上。

sentences.en: And is that because they can't afford it, they say?
sentences.zh: 他们是说因为负担不起吗？

sentences.en: That was the logic.
sentences.zh: 逻辑确实如此。

sentences.en: We're not spending money on this.
sentences.zh: 我们不能在这上面花钱。

sentences.en: But is this kind of ideological conviction that it will encourage welfarism and...
sentences.zh: 但这是否也是一种意识形态上的信念，认为这会助长福利依赖，并且……

sentences.en: And this is where we get into it.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们要深入探讨的地方。

sentences.en: This is where we get into the weeds of to what extent there's culpability in all of this.
sentences.zh: 我们要深入剖析这一切背后究竟有多少责任归属。

sentences.en: So there is an understanding of the gravity of the crisis.
sentences.zh: 当时人们对危机的严重性是有认知的。

sentences.en: And the gravity of the crisis is such that there are bodies such as the Quakers and there are charities who are sending money and arMs.
sentences.zh: 危机的严重程度促使了像贵格会这样的团体以及各种慈善机构开始寄送钱款和物资。

sentences.en: And they do incredible work.
sentences.zh: 他们做了了不起的工作。

sentences.en: And there is English people who send huge sums of money to help in this.
sentences.zh: 也有英国人寄出巨额资金来提供援助。

sentences.en: It goes to America where there are Irish emigrants already there because emigration to America was already enormous before the famine.
sentences.zh: 这些钱流向了美国，因为那里已经有爱尔兰移民了，毕竟在大饥荒之前，向美国的移民潮就已经非常庞大了。

sentences.en: And they are collecting money.
sentences.zh: 他们也在筹集资金。

sentences.en: And the Choctaw Indians most famously made a donation of the equivalent of about 5,000 pounds.
sentences.zh: 最著名的是乔克托印第安人捐赠了相当于约5000英镑的款项。

sentences.en: And this is the Choctaw Indians who had their own trail of tears from the 1830s.
sentences.zh: 要知道，乔克托印第安人自己在19世纪30年代也经历过“血泪之路”。

sentences.en: So they send money.
sentences.zh: 所以他们寄来了钱。

sentences.en: So everybody understands through this, through the reportage in the newspapers.
sentences.zh: 通过报纸的报道，每个人都了解这一切。

sentences.en: Nobody can possibly say that they don't know.
sentences.zh: 没有人能说自己不知道。

sentences.en: And the internal British correspondence flowing from Dublin Castle week after week over to England makes clear that there is an extraordinary crisis,
sentences.zh: 而且从都柏林城堡发往英国的内部通信，每周都在清楚地表明这是一场非同寻常的危机，

sentences.en: which is leading to daily death on an epic scale across Ireland during these years.
sentences.zh: 导致这些年间爱尔兰各地每天都在发生大规模的死亡。

sentences.en: And two aspects of this which really matters.
sentences.zh: 其中有两个方面非常重要。

sentences.en: The first is you have somebody like Charles Trevelyan, who is the chief of famine administrator in Ireland,
sentences.zh: 首先是像查尔斯·特里维廉这样的人，他是爱尔兰饥荒救济的总负责人，

sentences.en: who expresses desire that permanent good could come out of transient evil.
sentences.zh: 他曾表达过希望“从短暂的邪恶中产生永久的善”的愿望。

sentences.en: And that's this idea of famine as an austerity measure.
sentences.zh: 这就是将饥荒视为一种紧缩措施的观点。

sentences.en: And I don't wish to use a trite modern analogy for it, but it's the idea of providence.
sentences.zh: 我不想用陈腐的现代类比，但这其实就是“天意”的观念。

sentences.en: And the idea that it's Malthusian, basically, that a famine will clear out a population to make it more sustainable.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是马尔萨斯主义，认为饥荒可以清理人口，使之更具可持续性。

sentences.en: And he is the forebearer of Laura Trevelyan, BBC correspondent, who has now given money in reparations to people in the Caribbean because her family had plantations there.
sentences.zh: 他是BBC记者劳拉·特里维廉的先辈，劳拉现在已经向加勒比地区的人民支付了赔偿金，因为她的家族曾在那里拥有种植园。

sentences.en: And she's talking about doing it with this.
sentences.zh: 她现在也在谈论这件事。

sentences.en: And now she's saying, yeah.
sentences.zh: 她现在说，是的。

sentences.en: And it features in one of the most popular Irish ballads, the Fields of Aten Rye, where you stole Trevelyan's corn.
sentences.zh: 这出现在最受欢迎的爱尔兰民谣之一《阿滕莱原野》中，歌词里提到了你偷了特里维廉的玉米。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the young might see the born.
sentences.zh: 所以年轻人可能会看到……

sentences.en: So Trevelyan's corn was understood to be what was taken away.
sentences.zh: 所以特里维廉的玉米被理解为被掠夺走的粮食。

sentences.en: Now, it has to be said there were Irish farmers and Irish businessmen exporting food from Ireland during this thing.
sentences.zh: 当然，必须指出的是，当时确实有爱尔兰农民和商人在饥荒期间出口爱尔兰的粮食。

sentences.en: This is not a simple narrative, and that matters too, and it must be said.
sentences.zh: 这并不是一个简单的叙事，这一点也很重要，必须说出来。

sentences.en: But when it comes down to it, you have the Lord Lieutenant in Ireland writing to the British Prime Minister, Sir John Russell, to say in a letter very clearly,
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，爱尔兰总督在写给英国首相约翰·罗素爵士的信中非常明确地说道：

sentences.en: I do not think that there is another legislature in Europe that would disregard such suffering as now exists in the West of Ireland and coldly persist in a policy of extermination.
sentences.zh: “我不认为欧洲还有哪个立法机构会无视爱尔兰西部目前存在的苦难，并冷酷地坚持灭绝政策。”

sentences.en: Now, that is the leading British official in Ireland writing to the Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 这可是英国在爱尔兰的最高官员写给首相的信。

sentences.en: But that thing about a policy of extermination suggests a, I mean, at the very least, a genuine desire.
sentences.zh: 但关于“灭绝政策”的说法，至少暗示了一种真正的意图。

sentences.en: I mean, extermination is a big word.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，“灭绝”这个词太沉重了。

sentences.en: So there's a genuine desire among some English or British policymakers, you know, to pursue the line that you were just describing,
sentences.zh: 所以，一些英国政策制定者确实有一种真正的愿望，去推行你刚才描述的那种路线，

sentences.en: the idea that this is a necessary providential course that will, you know, I mean, I don't know how they would have put it,
sentences.zh: 即认为这是一种必要的天意过程，会……我不知道他们当时会怎么说，

sentences.en: winnow out the wheat from the chaff or get rid of the dead wood, or they would have used some equally kind of horrific expression.
sentences.zh: 也许是“去粗取精”或者“清除死木”，他们会用一些同样可怕的表达方式。

sentences.en: Or would they?
sentences.zh: 还是说他们会吗？

sentences.en: Or are we being unfair?
sentences.zh: 或者我们是否太不公平了？

sentences.en: I mean, is this what they thought?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们当时真的是这么想的吗？

sentences.en: That's as baldly as you can see it written, what I've just read out to you there.
sentences.zh: 我刚才读给你的内容，就是当时最直白的文字记录。

sentences.en: These ideas are current at the time, this idea, Malthusian ideas of population and what a population can be sustained on a place and what it means to a place to have a population.
sentences.zh: 这些思想在当时很流行，比如马尔萨斯关于人口的观点，关于一个地方能维持多少人口，以及拥有人口对一个地方意味着什么。

sentences.en: And how much of that, so in the last episode, we were talking about the 17th century and the stereotypes and the anxieties
sentences.zh: 那么，在上一集中，我们谈到了17世纪，谈到了克伦威尔的骑兵在跨越爱尔兰海时，

sentences.en: that Cromwell's troopers took with them when they crossed the Irish Sea.
sentences.zh: 随身携带的那些刻板印象和焦虑。

sentences.en: So how much of, I mean, I guess a lot of people would call it racist, wouldn't they?
sentences.zh: 所以，我想很多人会称之为种族主义，对吧？

sentences.en: How much of that plays into this?
sentences.zh: 这在多大程度上影响了这一切？

sentences.en: In other words, the fact that the people who are suffering Irish, does that make the British government's response
sentences.zh: 换句话说，受苦的人是爱尔兰人，这是否使得英国政府的反应

sentences.en: qualitatively different from if it had been in Yorkshire or in Wales or wherever?
sentences.zh: 与发生在约克郡、威尔士或其他地方的情况有着本质上的不同？

sentences.en: Well, I would say that within, to be frank about it, within the ruling classes of Britain at that time,
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，我认为在当时的英国统治阶级内部，

sentences.en: there was a disdain for working people, which can be seen through some of the treatment, through the Industrial Revolution, etc.
sentences.zh: 对劳动人民有一种蔑视，这可以从工业革命期间的一些对待方式中看出来。

sentences.en: However, the fact that it was in Ireland matters.
sentences.zh: 然而，发生在爱尔兰这一点很重要。

sentences.en: And it was separated by the sea.
sentences.zh: 它被大海隔开了。

sentences.en: It's a different landmass.
sentences.zh: 那是另一块陆地。

sentences.en: And there is centuries of just this idea that the Irish are not quite civilised or not civilised at all.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，一直存在着一种爱尔兰人不够文明，甚至根本不文明的观念。

sentences.en: And you can see it, it endures through the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到，这种观念贯穿了整个19世纪。

sentences.en: Over the last couple of weeks, I've been going back, reading newspapers before you guys came over and looking at Punch, for example.
sentences.zh: 过去几周，在你们过来之前，我一直在翻阅报纸，比如《笨拙》杂志。

sentences.en: Right, so the cartoons in that.
sentences.zh: 对，就是里面的漫画。

sentences.en: The cartoons in Punch.
sentences.zh: 《笨拙》杂志里的漫画。

sentences.en: And they bring you into a world of what can only be understood as popular representations of what the Irish were.
sentences.zh: 它们把你带入了一个世界，那只能被理解为当时对爱尔兰人形象的流行描绘。

sentences.en: By the way, those cartoons, I mean, or images like that are still appearing in British tabloid newspapers in the 1970s
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，那些漫画，或者类似的图像，在20世纪70年代的英国小报上还在出现，

sentences.en: when people are drawing Republican paramilitaries or something.
sentences.zh: 当时人们在画共和派准军事组织成员之类的东西。

sentences.en: They're drawing them in exactly the same way as wild, savage.
sentences.zh: 他们画的方式完全一样，都是野蛮、粗鲁的。

sentences.en: Yeah, simianised almost, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是的，几乎是猿猴化了，对吧？

sentences.en: Simian, exactly.
sentences.zh: 猿猴化，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And it is extraordinary when you look back at it, and it's jarring.
sentences.zh: 当你回看这些时，会感到非常震惊和刺眼。

sentences.en: And it's why there was a recent column by a cartoonist in the London Times, which again, just got a really bad reaction from here because it brought people back to that idea
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么《伦敦时报》最近有一位漫画家的专栏引起了这里强烈的反感，因为它让人们回想起了那种

sentences.en: of the representations of the Irish in the British popular press.
sentences.zh: 英国大众媒体对爱尔兰人的刻板印象。

sentences.en: And it matters, though.
sentences.zh: 但这很重要。

sentences.en: The famine matters, obviously.
sentences.zh: 饥荒显然很重要。

sentences.en: And the story of the famine isn't a million dead.
sentences.zh: 饥荒的故事不仅仅是百万人死亡。

sentences.en: It's the story of the famine is people dying on a ditch in the side of the road while they walk to Delphi Lodge looking for food.
sentences.zh: 饥荒的故事是人们在前往德尔菲小屋寻找食物的路上，死在路边的沟里。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because they're starving and being turned away and dying on the way back.
sentences.zh: 因为他们饿极了，却被拒之门外，在回来的路上死去了。

sentences.en: It's people being tossed over into the Atlantic Ocean where they die on a coffin ship on the way of cross.
sentences.zh: 是人们被扔进大西洋，死在横渡大洋的“棺材船”上。

sentences.en: And it matters for political reasons because it created a community of Irish people who were abroad, who could not be reconciled to the idea of the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 它在政治上很重要，因为它创造了一个流亡海外的爱尔兰人群体，他们无法接受联合王国的理念。

sentences.en: And the scale of those numbers of emigration are extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 而且移民的人数规模非常惊人。

sentences.en: You see, I had the impression that the aftermath of this coming on top of Cromwell and plantations and everything
sentences.zh: 你看，我原本以为在克伦威尔、种植园等一系列事件之后，饥荒的余波

sentences.en: was that in the wake of the famine, that Irish nationalism was Republican, was virulently
sentences.zh: 使得爱尔兰民族主义变得共和化，变得极其

sentences.en: Anglophobic, was absolutely committed to the overthrow of the Union, and that this was essentially
sentences.zh: 仇英，绝对致力于推翻联合，而这本质上就是

sentences.en: the Easter Rising and then the Revolution, was expressive of majority opinion in Ireland in the wake of the famine.
sentences.zh: 复活节起义以及随后的革命，表达了饥荒后爱尔兰的主流民意。

sentences.en: And I was kind of amazed to discover that wasn't the case at all, that actually the Republican
sentences.zh: 但我惊讶地发现事实并非如此，实际上，最终建立独立爱尔兰的共和

sentences.en: nationalism that ends up founding independent Ireland is a very, very minority pursuit, and that actually majority Irish nationalism does accept the functioning of the Union.
sentences.zh: 民族主义只是极少数人的追求，而大多数爱尔兰民族主义者实际上接受了联合王国的运作。

sentences.en: It wants home rule.
sentences.zh: 他们想要地方自治。

sentences.en: It wants a kind of a parliament, but one that would be subordinate to the Westminster Parliament.
sentences.zh: 他们想要一个议会，但要从属于威斯敏斯特议会。

sentences.en: In a weird way, the famine leaves a massive political and cultural scar, and one that will never heal, I guess, or one that will never disappear anyway.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，饥荒留下了一道巨大的政治和文化伤疤，我想这道伤疤永远不会愈合，或者至少永远不会消失。

sentences.en: But why doesn't it lead to greater political...
sentences.zh: 但为什么它没有导致更大的政治……

sentences.en: Yeah, because I'm really surprised by that.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为我对此感到非常惊讶。

sentences.en: Why actually is it so quiescent?
sentences.zh: 为什么它实际上如此平静？

sentences.en: Is it because the famine is so awful that people are too exhausted to...
sentences.zh: 是因为饥荒太可怕了，以至于人们精疲力竭到……

sentences.en: Why isn't there a revolution, an uprising, massive political turbulence?
sentences.zh: 为什么没有发生革命、起义或大规模的政治动荡？

sentences.en: Where you had Chris Clark on talking about the rebellions of 1848, there was a rebellion
sentences.zh: 你之前请克里斯·克拉克谈论1848年的叛乱，当时确实有

sentences.en: in Dublin in 1848 by young Irelanders, a movement who drew on ideas of a newspaper called The
sentences.zh: 1848年在都柏林由“青年爱尔兰人”发起的叛乱，这是一个受《国家报》思想启发的运动，
